Surat al-Jathiyah is Meccan. [Al-Suyuti, in al-Durr al-Manthur (7/422), attributes to Ibn Mardawayh, from Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: "The surah Ḥā Mīm al-Jāthiyah was revealed in Mecca."] In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful (﷽).

* *

﴿Ḥā Mīm. The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise. Indeed, in the heavens and the earth are signs for the believers. The others read both with a damma (rafʿ), as a fresh statement (istiʾnaf), since the Arabs say: "Inna lī ʿalayka mālan wa-ʿalā akhīka mālun" (I have wealth against you, and against your brother there is wealth), where they put the second in the accusative or the nominative. ﴿For a people who are certain﴾ that there is no god but Him.

The others read it with a yāʾ.

﴿Woe to every sinful liar﴾, a liar, possessor of sin, meaning: al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 45, verses 8–14:

﴿He hears the verses of Allah recited to him, then persists in arrogance as though he had not heard them. So give him the tidings of a painful punishment. And when he learns anything of Our verses,﴾ Muqatil said: "of the Qur'an," ﴿he takes them in mockery. For such there is a humiliating punishment.﴾ It is mentioned in the plural form, referring back to "every" in His saying: ﴿Woe to every sinful liar.﴾

﴿Before them is Hell,﴾ meaning: ﴿before them﴾ is ahead of them, ﴿Hell﴾. This means that they are in this world ([enjoying their wealth]) [[The words between the brackets are not present in the two manuscripts, but the meaning requires them, and they are present in the printed edition.]], and in the Hereafter they have the Fire, which they will enter. ﴿Neither what they earned will avail them at all,﴾ of wealth, ﴿nor those they took as protectors besides Allah,﴾ nor what they worshipped besides Allah of deities. ﴿And for them is a great punishment.﴾

﴿This﴾ means this Qur'an, ﴿is a guidance﴾, a clarification from error. ﴿And those who disbelieve in the signs of their Lord, for them is a punishment of painful wrath.﴾

﴿It is Allah who subjected the sea to you, so that ships may sail upon it by His command, and that you may seek of His bounty, and that perhaps you will be grateful. And He subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, all of it from Him.﴾ The meaning of its subjection is that He created it for our benefits, so it is subjected to us insofar as we benefit from it. ﴿All of it from Him﴾: so do not set up rivals to Allah. Ibn Abbas said: "All of it from Him" — all of that is a mercy from Him. Al-Zajjaj said: all of that is a bounty and kindness from Him.

﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect.﴾

﴿Say to those who believe: forgive those who do not expect the Days of Allah.﴾ That is, they do not fear the events of Allah and do not care about His vengeance. Ibn Abbas and Muqatil said: it was revealed concerning Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, because a man from the Banu Ghifar reviled him in Makkah, so Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, intended to seize him, and Allah revealed this verse and commanded him to pardon him [[See: Zad al-Masir: 7/358.]].

Al-Qurazi and al-Suddi said: it was revealed concerning some people among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from the people of Makkah, who were suffering severe harm from the polytheists before they were commanded to fight. They complained of that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so Allah revealed this verse [[See: Zad al-Masir: 7/358, and he attributed it together with the previous report to al-Baghawi.]]. Then the verse of fighting abrogated it (naskh) [[See what preceded: 3/32.]].

﴿That He may recompense a people﴾: Ibn Amir, Hamza and al-Kisa'i recited "linajziya" with the nun, and the others recited it with the ya, meaning "li-yajziya Allah" (that Allah may recompense). Abu Ja'far recited "liyujza" with a damma on the first ya, a sukun on the second, and a fatha on the zay. Abu Amr said: this is a solecism (lahn, a grammatical error). Al-Kisa'i said: its meaning is that the recompense may recompense a people, ﴿for what they used to earn.﴾

Al-Sha'bi said: Desire (al-hawa) is so named only because it plunges (yahwi) its companion into the Fire [[See: al-Qurtubi: 16/167.]].

Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "ghishwah" with a fatha on the ghayn and a sukun on the shin, while the rest read "ghishawah", meaning a darkness, so he does not see guidance. ﴿Then who can guide him after Allah?﴾ [that is, who can guide him] after Allah has led him astray. ﴿Will you not then be mindful?﴾

(2247): 4/1763; and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 12/355.]].

This is the commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 45, verses 29–32:

﴿This is Our Record; it speaks against you with truth﴾ — meaning the register of the recording angels (diwan al-hafazah), ﴿it speaks against you with truth﴾, bearing witness against you with a clear and sufficient explanation, as if it were speaking. And it was said: the intended "Record" is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).

﴿Indeed, We used to have copied down what you used to do﴾ — that is, We commanded the angels to copy (nasq) your deeds, meaning to write them down and record them against you.

And it was said: "nastansikh" means We take a copy of it (nuskhatahu). This is because the two angels raise up the deeds of a person, and then Allah affirms from them what had reward or punishment for him, and discards from them what is vain, such as their saying: "Come here" and "Go away."

And it was said: copying (al-istinsakh) is from the Preserved Tablet; the angels copy each year what will occur of the deeds of the children of Adam, and copying is only from an original, so one book is copied from another.

Al-Dahhak said: "nastansikh" means "We establish" (nuthbit). Al-Suddi said: "We write" (naktub). Al-Hasan said: "We preserve" (nahfaz).

﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, their Lord will admit them into His mercy. That is the manifest triumph.﴾ [al-Zafar] [[Addition from "b".]] al-Zahir.

﴿As for those who disbelieved﴾ it will be said to them, ﴿Were not My verses recited to you? But you were arrogant, and you were a criminal people﴾ — arrogant and disbelieving.

﴿And when it was said, "Indeed, the promise of Allah is true, and the Hour, there is no doubt about it," you said, "We do not know what the Hour is; we only assume an assumption, and we are not certain."﴾ Hamzah read "wa-al-sa'ah" with a fatha, placing it in coordination with "the promise," while the others read it with a damma as a nominative beginning (mubtada'). ﴿We only assume an assumption﴾ — meaning we know nothing of that except by conjecture and supposition.

﴿And we are not certain﴾ that it will occur.
